title: Railstrip: single-row observability rail for onboarding — latency / cost / trace peek
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a compact, horizontally oriented 'railstrip' UI component to surface the most critical observability signals for first-time users. The railstrip is intended for the onboarding quickstart: a single-row, left-to-right summary of recent latency percentile, cost-per-token spark, and a tappable trace peek that opens a lightweight waterfall modal. Deliverables: annotated screenshots for docs, three responsive breakpoints, export-ready PNGs, and a copy-ready spec for the engineering handoff.
acceptance_criteria: Three annotated screenshot variants (desktop, tablet, mobile) exported as 2x PNGs
Railstrip component spec with spacing, type, and color tokens in Figma (dev-ready)
Trace peek interaction documented with animation timeline and keyboard accessibility notes
Design handoff PR opened with image assets, figma link, and screenshot captions for docs team
design_notes: Principles: keep the rail lightweight and scannable, prioritize latency and cost signals first, then provide an affordance to expand to a trace view. Trade-offs: we compress metrics to micro-sparklines to avoid visual noise; we avoid showing raw token values by default to reduce cognitive load. Accessibility: ensure 3:1 contrast for sparkline strokes and provide screen-reader labels for each segment. Engineering constraints discovered: waterfall modal must lazy-load trace payload to avoid blocking the onramp experience. Follow-on work will be a11y testing with VoiceOver and TalkBack.
